title: Jump Detection, the Weierstrass Bridge, and the Plateau Staircase on E: y2 = x3 + 7
content: For the CM elliptic curve E: y2 = x3 + 7 over ℝ and the point P0 = (2, √15), we study the orbit {[K]P0} through the Weierstrass parametrization of E(ℝ) by the circle ℝ/ℤ. We prove: (i) a jump characterization of the elliptic logarithm: the boundary value of log(℘ − x) has exactly one jump, of size −iπ, on the real half-period, which yields a quadrature-free bisection for τ(x); (ii) a Sokhotski–Plemelj decomposition of a Mellin-type integral whose imaginary part is −π z(x)s−1; (iii) the Lattès formula x([1 − ζ3]P) = −ζ32(x3 + 28)/(3x2) from the group law; (iv) that P0 has infinite order and that convergent denominators qk of u0 = τ0/ω with 3 | qk give indices K = qk/3 at which [K]P0 is within 1/(3qk+1) of a 3-torsion point; (v) a first-order relation |ψ3(x([K]P0))| = 84ω√7 d3(K) + O(d3(K)2) between the division polynomial and the torus distance to E[3]. We compute the record (“plateau”) indices for approach to O, E[2] and E[3] up to K = 1.2 × 106 and show that, beyond the convergent-type indices, the 3-torsion records include other best approximations. Finally we recall that on E(ℝ) the discrete logarithm reduces to the classical inhomogeneous approximation problem for u0, solved by Ostrowski numeration; this is the real-analytic elliptic logarithm method and has no bearing on the discrete logarithm over finite fields.
